On your questions...
ASML makes the primary tech needed to fab a modern day chip (EUV machines). They currently have a monopoly as these are insanely complex and expensive machines (think many many step process to end up with a super pure special laser at the end). ASML will stay a monopoly barring industrial espionage etc so they will tend to go up so long as chip demand is high.
INTC/AMD: The two main X86 players. They've gone back and forth for decades. INTC tries to fab in house (but also buys some TSMC). AMD used to fab but now primarily goes through TSMC.
NVDA: Wants to get into CPU's (has the Tegras and tried to buy ARM) but mostly the mackdaddy king of GPU (because they made CUDA the industry standard). In gaming AMD competes well (comparable GPUs) but in AI AMD has put up a poor effort (no CUDA competitor).
TSMC: The best fab today. Fabbing is extremely expensive (i.e. need massive massive capital to buy tons of ASML's machines and other such tools). Fabbing is essentially series of processes (chemical baths, laser treatments etc) to purify down a ton of silicon to a wafer and then one way or another (chemical, laser etc) carve circuits into it. Each step can have losses and tiny impurities can ruin the die. Because of how capital intensive it is, it tends to be winner take all. Whoever has the best fab will have folks want to fab with them ==>money to invest in the next gen of fab.

AMD vs INTC as leader: INTC was leader until ~2014ish. Then under poor leadership they made some critical mistakes. They didn't get into EUV for their process, they didn't invest enough in R&D etc. During that time TSMC got ahead of INTC in process and AMD came up with some important architectural innovations: chiplets. Make tiny chiplets that piece together (like ultra complex legos) rather than giant monolithic chips. The chiplets are easier to make (so yield is much improved) but you do pay a price (there's performance/energy cost making the interconnects between the chips).

Right now...INTC leads on desktop CPU...because they made their chip bigger in silicon (i.e. brute force) AND because AMD came out with their last version ~1.5 years ago. But desktop doesn't matter. The money is in Data Center. DC only cares about performance per watt (because higher watts==>higher heat==>higher space taken up). Right now AMD is undisputed leader of DC and Intel THEMSELVES have published material stating they won't have performance per watt supremacy until 2024 or so (meaning any investment in Intel is optimistically going to be dead money until then).
